note: Known differences between the Node CI domain (goldens/ci.json) and the Go one that are decisions, not bugs: ingest hardening of the artifact integers and cost (NFR6003/NFR6004, security note of the W1 contract notes) and the zip integrity check. TestCIArtifactParity and TestCIZipParity fail when a listed case starts to agree, when an unlisted case disagrees and when a listed value changes. Consumer: ci_test.go.

deviations.reason: Go-only hardening (NFR6003, ingest): integer fields are limited to JavaScript's safe range (2^53-1) because they are stored in integer columns; Node's zod int() accepts 1e21. The artifact is skipped as artifact_invalid instead of failing the insert on every refresh.
Same hardening as 'counts 1e21': integers above 2^53-1 are refused so a hostile artifact cannot make the insert fail on every refresh.
Go-only hardening: a cost that overflows to infinity is refused (it cannot be stored in the numeric cost column); Node's parse yields Infinity, which its schema accepts.

Node does not check the CRC-32 of an entry and returns the corrupted bytes (which then fail the schema: artifact_invalid); the Go reader verifies length and CRC-32 and refuses the entry. The artifact outcome is the same (zips/ case agrees).
